source_records.title: Deligne’s numbered errata and convention changes
source_records.as_he_states: The letter proposes weaker assumptions at0.16.1.9,0.19.4.6/7,0.20.4.13; inserts local at0.19.8.3; reverses the universal-differential sign; rejects III4.3.6’s displayed completion formula.
source_records.plausible_today: Each is a separate edition-specific check; a sign convention is not a false theorem, and a suggested weakening is not an already established erratum.
source_records.state_of_art: Three exact checks are now complete. Printed0.16.1.9 p24 assumes noetherianity; its dimension equality extends without it because the faithful finite-module determinant trick makes B/Ann_B(M) integral over A/Ann_A(M), and integral extensions preserve dimension. Printed0.19.8.3 pp110–111 claims uniqueness among homomorphisms from a prime local ring: locality is essential, since every Z_(p) maps nonlocally to Q. Printed0.20.4.13(iv) p127 has the integral-closure hypothesis; localization gives Omega_B/A tensor Frac(B)=Omega_Frac(B)/Frac(A)=0 for an algebraic separable fraction extension, without integral closure. The0.20.4.6 sign is a convention requiring coherent propagation. The19.4.6–7 simplification proposals are not independently certified. Original EGAIII1,4.3.6 printedp133, has the alleged false equality. For A=Q[x,y]_(x,y), the prime (y−(exp(x)−1)) in Ahat contracts to0 and survives localization by A minus0, so Frac(A) tensor_A Ahat is not a field. The desired analytically-integral implies unibranch argument nevertheless works with the natural inclusion into Frac(Ahat). Full details are in proof_notes.md §11. The later published errata confirm the first three corrections and record the sign change, subject to the printed old/new-label transposition just described. Exact later errata: EGA IV4 Liste 3 de corrections, IV nos.6,9,12–14, printed pp.347–348 (1967). No.6 removes noetherianity from 0.16.1.9; no.9 inserts local in 0.19.8.3/4; nos.12–13 change the differential convention; no.14 removes integral closure in 0.20.4.13(iv) and supplies a denominator-clearing argument. The first p1/p2 instruction in no.12 itself has old/new labels reversed relative to the original p.125; its explicit tensor formula and no.13 determine the intended change. The 19.4.6–7 suggested proof simplifications remain separate bounded verification questions. The III4.3.6 equality is now verified false in the original print, while its conclusion is independently recovered using the natural injection.

source_records.worth: Worth a line-level errata concordance; no mathematical novelty claim is justified by numbering alone.

title: Deligne’s deferred hard-Lefschetz proof request
as_he_states: In his letter of17October1966, Deligne says he will not attempt to prove the named théorème de Lefschetz vache that year and hopes Grothendieck finds someone who will. The sentence supplies no further hypotheses.
plausible_today: The historical sentence requests a proof of the named theorem without specifying a base field, coefficients or smoothness/projectivity hypotheses. The exact terminology in SGA7 XVIII5.2.2 identifies the standard hard-Lefschetz interpretation: for X smooth projective of pure dimension n over an algebraically closed field k, an ample invertible sheaf L, and a prime l different from char(k), cup product with c1(L)^i gives an isomorphism H^(n-i)(X,Q_l) -> H^(n+i)(X,Q_l(i)) for every i>=0. This precise statement is the later matched theorem, not a transcription of hypotheses from the letter.
state_of_art: SGA7II XVIII5.2.2 and5.2.2.1, printed pp281–282, use exactly the name Lefschetz vache for the cup-product isomorphisms and still conjecture the smooth case. The exposé is by N.Katz, expressly based on succinct Grothendieck notes (printed p254). Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, Theorem4.1.1 and proof4.1.2–4.1.4, printed pp217–218, establish the stated smooth-projective Q_l theorem. The letter is dated17October1966; SGA7II was published1973; WeilII was received1June1979 and published in volume52(1980), with Numdam catalogue date28December1980. No exact first-circulation date is established. ClassB records establishment by another author relative to Grothendieck: Pierre Deligne, who also wrote the attached letter. Neither letter nor theorem is attributed to Grothendieck.
why_open: The source explicitly defers Deligne’s attempt for that year and asks that someone else undertake it. It states no mathematical reason for the deferral; the subsequent mention of convalescent EGA reading is not treated as a causal explanation.
worth: Worth retaining as a dated historical request with a later exact theorem match; the standard smooth-projective Q_l theorem is settled and does not warrant a new proof task here.
